content.text: Timme’s *Der Empfindsame* satirizes German sentimentalism, distinguishing genuine feeling from exaggerated imitation of Sterne, Werther, and Siegwart. The later narrative follows Perth amid noble rivalries, religious reform, and violence. Henry Smith escorts Louise from the Dominican monastery through secret passages and the garden, then shelters her in his kitchen before leaving for Simon Glover’s house. Royal leaders meet in the monastery’s council room, debating Highland warfare and heresy. Catharine and Father Clement meet on Kinnoull Hill; Highland chief Eachin arrives and escorts Clement toward the Highlands. In Ramorny’s sick chamber, Dwining and Bonthron plot revenge; Bonthron kills Oliver Proudfute outside Smith’s house. Perth’s citizens gather around the corpse, mistakenly believing Smith dead, while Catharine runs to Smith’s house and collapses in his arms.
